questions: How does the CLI handle disabled goal endpoints today?
What is the full ungated Goals CLI surface?
Should the CLI pre-check feature flags or handle server errors reactively?

answers.answer: It does not handle them at all. Goals commands hit server API directly with no pre-check. If the server returns an error, the CLI shows raw HTTP error messages via the generic error parsing in goals/utils.ts. There is no feature-flag-specific error handling.
evidence: src/goals/index.ts:20 — runGoals dispatches subcommands with no feature check
src/index.ts:124-127 — hlx goals always routed to runGoals
src/goals/utils.ts — generic error parsing, no feature-flag handling

answers.answer: 5 subcommands always available: create, list, get, terminate, resume. All dispatched unconditionally from the goals router. Documentation for all commands in cli-content.ts:133-176.
evidence: src/goals/index.ts:28-89 — switch dispatches create, list, get, terminate, resume
src/goals/create.ts, list.ts, get.ts, terminate.ts, resume.ts — individual command files

answers.answer: Reactive handling is simpler and sufficient. When the server returns 404 for goal endpoints (because GOALS_ENABLED=false), the CLI should detect that specific error pattern and display a user-friendly message like 'Goals feature is not enabled on this server'. This avoids adding a pre-flight check endpoint and keeps the CLI stateless with respect to feature flags.
evidence: src/lib/config.ts — CLI config has no feature flag env vars; adding one would create dual state
src/goals/utils.ts — existing error parsing utility can be extended for feature-flag errors
Ticket intent: single server env var, not per-client configuration

statement: The CLI has 5 goals subcommands always available with no feature-flag gating. When the server starts returning 404 for disabled goal endpoints, the CLI needs to catch that response and display a user-friendly disabled message rather than raw HTTP errors. The simplest approach is reactive error handling in the goals command dispatcher or shared utility.
